The Gunung Kurau cave did not give very reliable results as the layers appear to have become shifted time and again by the floods of the Kurau river. However it produced two good implements of a middle-neolithic culture, one of them even belonging to a late period of this stage.

Of the Pahang-caves, that in Gunung SSnum proved to be the most interesting as it produced, besides four palaeoliths chipped on both sides, two good proto-neoliths and part of the edge of a real neolithic implement belonging to the earlier period of the Upper Neolithic. The same site also gave cord-marked pottery, red and black haematite and grinding-stones coloured with the red paint.
